changelog: [Core Principles]: added three precise WHERE-conditions targeting the critic's measured wrong-boundary/over-segmentation cases — never strand a verb-less trailing fragment, never isolate a single filler word as its own segment, and place the boundary BEFORE a reporting/quotative connective (e.g. -했더니) rather than after it — folded into the existing 'when in doubt, split' bullet so these read as conditions on WHERE a safe cut sits, not blanket bans on any connective form. This avoids repeating the rejected v3 change, which added the same ideas to [Never Segment]+[Decision Procedure] and over-restricted latency; here they are scoped narrowly (verb-less trailing fragment, single-word filler, reporting connective) with no effect on ordinary clause splits.

[When to Segment]: added five concrete permissive cues directly answering the critic's under-segmentation evidence (missed_gain cases that already passed the quality floor): causal -어서/아서 when both sides are independently complete, sequential 나중에/-고 나서 markers, opinion-introducing phrases like 내 생각에는, embedded '?' followed by an independent resumption clause, and a topic-shifting 이제 immediately before a self-contained final clause. These are stated as general surface conditions, not sentence-specific rules, and target boundaries INSIDE previously-unsplit long sentences rather than adding more short pieces elsewhere.
